nodes.summary: Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real random variables on a probability space and $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$. If almost surely $S_n = 0$ for every $n$, then almost surely there is $l \in \mathbb{R}$ with $S_n \to l$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: A zero walk converges to a finite limit

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\Omega$ and let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real-valued functions on $\Omega$, with partial sums $S_n = \sum_{i\lt n} X_i$. If for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$ we have $X_i(\omega) = 0$ for all $i$, then for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$ the sequence $S_n(\omega)$ converges to a finite real limit.
nodes.title: Vanishing steps give a convergent random walk

nodes.summary: Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real random variables on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ and $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$. The random walk $(S_n)$ converges to a finite limit if for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$ there is $l \in \mathbb{R}$ with $S_n(\omega) \to l$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Random walk with a finite limit

nodes.summary: For $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th coordinate is the map $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}} \to \mathbb{R}$ sending a real sequence $\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots)$ to its $i$-th term $\omega_i$.
nodes.title: Coordinate process on sequence space

nodes.summary: Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real random variables on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ and $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$. The random walk $(S_n)$ drifts to $-\infty$ if for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$, $S_n(\omega) \to -\infty$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Random walk drifting to $-\infty$

nodes.summary: Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real random variables on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ and $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$. The random walk $(S_n)$ drifts to $+\infty$ if for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$, $S_n(\omega) \to +\infty$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Random walk drifting to $+\infty$

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$ and let $F : \Omega \to [-\infty, +\infty]$ be measurable. If for every real $a$ the set $\{\omega : F(\omega) \le a\}$ has $\mu$-measure $0$ or $1$, then there is $c \in [-\infty, +\infty]$ with $F = c$ $\mu$-almost everywhere.
nodes.title: Zero–one sublevel sets force an almost surely constant variable

nodes.summary: For every real $c$ and every real sequence $(u_n)$, with limits inferior taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$, $\liminf_{n \to \infty} (c + u_n) = c + \liminf_{n \to \infty} u_n$.
nodes.title: Liminf commutes with adding a constant

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\mathbb{N}$ that moves only finitely many points. For every real sequence $\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots)$, the limit inferior in $[-\infty, +\infty]$ of the partial sums $\sum_{i\lt n} \omega_{\sigma(i)}$ equals the limit inferior of the partial sums $\sum_{i\lt n} \omega_i$.
nodes.title: Finite permutations do not change the liminf of the partial sums

nodes.summary: If a real sequence $(S_n)$ tends to $+\infty$, then its limit inferior in the extended reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$ is $+\infty$.
nodes.title: A real sequence tending to $+\infty$ has liminf $+\infty$

nodes.summary: For a real sequence $\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots)$ write $S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i\lt n} \omega_i$, and let $\omega'$ be its shift, $\omega'_i = \omega_{i+1}$. Then, with limits inferior taken in $[-\infty, +\infty]$, we have $\liminf_{n \to \infty} S_n(\omega) = \omega_0 + \liminf_{n \to \infty} S_n(\omega')$.
nodes.title: One-step shift identity for the liminf of the partial sums

nodes.summary: For every sequence $(u_n)$ in the extended reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$, $\liminf_{n \to \infty} u_{n+1} = \liminf_{n \to \infty} u_n$.
nodes.title: Dropping the first term does not change the liminf

nodes.summary: For every real $c$ and every real sequence $(u_n)$, with limits superior taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$, $\limsup_{n \to \infty} (c + u_n) = c + \limsup_{n \to \infty} u_n$.
nodes.title: Limsup commutes with adding a constant

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\mathbb{N}$ that moves only finitely many points. For every real sequence $\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots)$, the limit superior in $[-\infty, +\infty]$ of the partial sums $\sum_{i\lt n} \omega_{\sigma(i)}$ equals the limit superior of the partial sums $\sum_{i\lt n} \omega_i$.
nodes.title: Finite permutations do not change the limsup of the partial sums

nodes.summary: Let $(S_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of real numbers with $S_n \to -\infty$ as $n \to \infty$. Then the limit superior of $(S_n)$, taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$, equals $-\infty$.
nodes.title: A sequence tending to $-\infty$ has limsup $-\infty$

nodes.summary: For a real sequence $\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots)$ write $S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i < n} \omega_i$, and let $\theta\omega = (\omega_1, \omega_2, \dots)$ be the one-step shift. Then for every $\omega$, $\limsup_{n \to \infty} S_n(\omega) = \omega_0 + \limsup_{n \to \infty} S_n(\theta\omega)$, where both limits superior are taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$.
nodes.title: One-step shift identity for the limsup of partial sums

nodes.summary: For every sequence $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of extended reals, $\limsup_{n \to \infty} u_{n+1} = \limsup_{n \to \infty} u_n$.
nodes.title: Dropping the first term preserves the limsup

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$, and let $\rho^{\otimes \mathbb{N}}$ be the product measure on the sequence space $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$. The image of $\rho^{\otimes \mathbb{N}}$ under the one-step shift $(\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots) \mapsto (\omega_1, \omega_2, \dots)$ is $\rho^{\otimes \mathbb{N}}$.
nodes.title: Shift invariance of the i.i.d. product measure

nodes.summary: Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real-valued functions on a set $\Omega$, and for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$ be the smallest σ-algebra on $\Omega$ for which every $X_i$ with $i \ge n$ is Borel measurable. For all $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$, the function $\omega \mapsto \sum_{n \le i < m} X_i(\omega)$ is measurable with respect to $\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$.

nodes.summary: Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real-valued functions on a set $\Omega$, and for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$ be the smallest σ-algebra on $\Omega$ for which every $X_i$ with $i \ge n$ is Borel measurable. If $n \le i$, then $X_i$ is measurable with respect to $\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$.

Then the event that $\limsup_{m \to \infty} S_m = +\infty$ and $\liminf_{m \to \infty} S_m = -\infty$, with the limit superior and inferior taken in the extended reals, belongs to the tail σ-algebra of $X$.

nodes.summary: Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real random variables on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ and $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$. The random walk $(S_n)$ oscillates if for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$, $\limsup_n S_n(\omega) = +\infty$ and $\liminf_n S_n(\omega) = -\infty$, the limits taken in the extended reals.
nodes.title: Oscillating random walk

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\mathbb{N}$ with $\sigma(m) = m$ for every $m \ge N$. Then for every real sequence $(\omega_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ and every $n \ge N$, $\sum_{i < n} \omega_{\sigma(i)} = \sum_{i < n} \omega_i$.
nodes.title: Partial sums are unchanged by permuting the first coordinates

nodes.summary: Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be independent, identically distributed real random variables on a probability space and $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$. Then one of the following events has probability one: $S_n = 0$ for every $n$; $S_n \to +\infty$; $S_n \to -\infty$; or $\limsup_n S_n = +\infty$ and $\liminf_n S_n = -\infty$.
nodes.title: Random-walk dichotomy

nodes.summary: Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be independent, identically distributed real random variables on a probability space and $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$. Then one of the following events has probability one: $S_n$ converges to a finite limit (which may depend on the outcome); $S_n \to +\infty$; $S_n \to -\infty$; or $\limsup_n S_n = +\infty$ and $\liminf_n S_n = -\infty$.

nodes.summary: For a sequence of functions $X_i : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th partial sum is $S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i < n} X_i(\omega)$, the position at time $n$ of the random walk on $\mathbb{R}$ with increments $X_i$.

nodes.title: Limsup minus infinity forces divergence to minus infinity

nodes.summary: Let $(S_n)$ be a sequence of real numbers. If $\liminf_{n \to \infty} S_n = +\infty$ in the extended reals, then $S_n \to +\infty$ as $n \to \infty$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, let $X_0, X_1, \ldots$ be real-valued functions on $\Omega$, and let $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$ be the partial sums of the random walk. The walk is a zero walk when, for $\mu$-almost every $\omega \in \Omega$, we have $S_n(\omega) = 0$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
